# Specification: Crew Chatter MVP

## Summary

This spec covers the first release of Crew Chatter, a web app for personal notes. It includes email/password authentication with strict per-user ownership; note creation and rich-text editing with debounced auto-save; a notes dashboard; nested folders; color-coded tags; full-text search with filters; pinning; archive and trash with restore; checklists with progress; attachments; version history with restore; single-note and full-collection export; Markdown/plain-text import with a review step; and desktop and mobile web layouts.

## Repository context

- Monorepo using npm workspaces `backend` and `frontend` (root `package.json`).
- Backend: Express + TypeScript (ESM, `module` ES2020, `moduleResolution` bundler), PostgreSQL 16 via `pg`, with `bcryptjs`, `jsonwebtoken`, `multer`, `archiver` and `pdfkit` already installed. Relative imports in backend source use explicit `.js` extensions so the emitted ESM runs under Node.
- Frontend: React 18 + Vite + Tailwind CSS 4 + TipTap 3 + TanStack Query + Zustand + Radix UI, all already installed. `frontend/src/App.tsx`, `README.md` and `backend/.env.example` already exist and are modified rather than created.
- The database schema is defined in TypeScript (`backend/src/db/schema.ts`) and applied by `backend/src/db/migrate.ts` when the server starts, so no SQL file sits outside the type-checked sources.
- Password-reset links are sent by email over SMTP, configured through `backend/.env.example`. This requires an email library dependency. Attachments and export archives are stored in a server-local directory outside the web root, with downloads authorized through the API; the directory path is set in `backend/.env.example`.
- Repository files establish what each verification command checks. `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` over `backend/src`. `npm run lint` runs ESLint over `backend/src` (`.ts`) and `frontend/src` (`.ts`, `.tsx`; react-hooks rules enabled). `npm run build` runs `tsc` in the backend, emitting to `backend/dist`, and `tsc && vite build` in the frontend (`noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` enabled), emitting to `frontend/dist`. Both `dist/` directories and `*.tsbuildinfo` are gitignored. Every declared `.ts`/`.tsx` artifact must therefore type-check under its workspace tsconfig and pass that workspace's ESLint config. The SMTP email library is the one new npm dependency; the implementation must add it to the workspace `package.json` and the root `package-lock.json` together so `npm ci` succeeds. Any other added dependency must be handled the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Submitting the registration form with an email that has no account and a password creates an account and shows that user's notes dashboard in a signed-in state.
- AC-002: Submitting the registration form with an email that already has an account shows an error message and does not create a second account for that email.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password shows the notes dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password shows an error message and does not show the dashboard.
- AC-004: After the user clicks sign out, the sign-in screen is shown, and reloading the app shows the sign-in screen rather than the dashboard.
- AC-005: After a user requests a password reset for a registered email and completes it with a new password, signing in with the new password succeeds and signing in with the old password fails.
- AC-006: Every API request to a notes, folders, tags, checklist items, attachments, versions, search, export, or import endpoint made without a valid session returns HTTP 401.
- AC-007: When user B requests, updates, or deletes a note, folder, tag, checklist item, attachment, version, or preference setting owned by user A, or assigns user A's folder or tag to a note of user B, the API returns HTTP 403 or 404 (HTTP 400, 403, or 404 for the assignment), user A's resource is unchanged, and no cross-owner association is created.
- AC-008: For user B, the note list, search results, folder tree, tag list, and full-collection export contain none of user A's notes, folders, tags, or attachments.
- AC-009: For a registered user, no stored column value in that user's account record equals or contains the plaintext password they registered with.
- AC-010: Clicking "New note" on the dashboard creates a note and opens it in the editor with keyboard focus in the title or body field.
- AC-011: Pressing the new-note keyboard shortcut while on the dashboard creates a note and opens it in the editor with keyboard focus in the title or body field.
- AC-012: The editor applies each of heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote, and code block formatting, and each applied format is still present after the note is reloaded.
- AC-013: After the user stops typing in a note, an auto-save request for the change is sent no earlier than 500 ms and no later than 1,000 ms after the last keystroke, and the editor has no manual save button.
- AC-014: The save-status indicator shows "Saving" while an auto-save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Offline" while the browser reports no network connection, and "Unable to save" after a save request fails.
- AC-015: Reloading the page after the save-status indicator shows "Saved" displays the note with exactly the title and body last typed.
- AC-016: Closing the tab or navigating the browser away while an auto-save is pending or in flight triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation prompt.
- AC-017: Switching to another note within the app while an edit's auto-save is pending, then reopening the first note, shows the edited content.
- AC-018: A note whose title and body contain emoji, CJK characters, and right-to-left script text displays that text unchanged after it is saved and reloaded.
- AC-019: Pasting content copied from a web page or from a document editor into a note inserts its text, and that text is unchanged after the note is saved and reloaded.
- AC-020: A note saved with an empty title is labeled "Untitled note" in the note list and in search results.
- AC-021: A note's created_at is set when it is created and its updated_at changes to a later time after each saved edit.
- AC-022: The dashboard shows a pinned-notes section and a recent-notes list ordered by last updated date with the newest first.
- AC-023: The note list sort control offers last updated date, creation date, title, and pinned status, and selecting each option reorders the displayed notes by that field.
- AC-024: Each note card or row displays the note's title, a content preview, its tags, its folder name, and its last updated timestamp.
- AC-025: A signed-in user who has no notes sees an empty state on the dashboard containing a control that creates their first note.
- AC-026: A user can create a folder, create a subfolder inside it, and rename either one, and the sidebar folder tree shows each change after a page reload.
- AC-027: A user can change the order of sibling folders, and the new order is shown in the sidebar after a page reload.
- AC-028: Each folder that has subfolders can be collapsed in the sidebar tree to hide its subfolders and expanded to show them.
- AC-029: Selecting a folder in the sidebar lists every note assigned directly to that folder that is neither archived nor in trash, and lists no note assigned to a folder outside that folder and its subfolders.
- AC-030: Deleting a folder that contains notes prompts the user to choose between moving those notes to another folder and leaving them uncategorized, and after confirmation every contained note is in the chosen destination.
- AC-031: From the editor, a user can assign a note to a folder, move it to a different folder, and remove it from its folder so it is uncategorized, and each assignment is shown after a page reload.
- AC-032: A user can add multiple tags to one note, and every added tag is shown on the note's card and in the editor.
- AC-033: A tag created while tagging one note can be selected on another note, and the user's tag list then contains that tag exactly once.
- AC-034: Adding a tag named "Work" when the user already has a tag named "work" leaves the user with exactly one tag with that name ignoring case, and renaming a tag to a case-insensitive duplicate of another of the user's tags is rejected with an error message.
- AC-035: Two different users can each own a tag with the same name.
- AC-036: A user can set a tag's color, and the tag is displayed in that color on note cards and in the editor.
- AC-037: Renaming a tag changes its displayed name on every note carrying it, and deleting a tag removes it from every note without deleting any note.
- AC-038: Selecting a tag filters the note list to exactly the notes carrying that tag.
- AC-040: Pressing Cmd+K on macOS or Ctrl+K on other platforms opens global search with keyboard focus in the search field.
- AC-041: Searching for a word that appears only in a note's title returns that note, and searching for a word that appears only in a note's body returns that note.
- AC-042: For a query that matches a note's body, the search result shows a text excerpt in which the matching term is visually highlighted.
- AC-043: Search results can be narrowed by folder, tag, date range, note status, and attachment presence, and each applied filter removes every result that does not satisfy it.
- AC-044: Selecting a search result opens that note in the editor.
- AC-045: The note list can be filtered by folder, tag, pinned state, archived state, open tasks, and date range, and each filter shows exactly the notes that satisfy it.
- AC-046: A pinned note is listed above all unpinned notes on the dashboard and in its folder view and shows a pin indicator that unpinned notes do not show.
- AC-047: Unpinning a note removes its pin indicator and places it among unpinned notes in the current sort order.
- AC-048: A "Pinned" filter or sidebar destination lists exactly the user's pinned notes that are not in trash.
- AC-049: Archiving a note removes it from the dashboard, folder views, and tag views and lists it when the note list is filtered to archived notes, and unarchiving it returns it to those views.
- AC-050: Moving a note to trash removes it from every view except the Trash view.
- AC-051: Clicking "Restore" on a trashed note whose original folder still exists returns the note to that folder and shows a confirmation message.
- AC-052: Restoring a trashed note whose original folder has been deleted places the note in the uncategorized note list and shows a confirmation message.
- AC-053: A trashed note that has been in trash longer than the trash retention period is permanently deleted, and a trashed note still within that period can be restored.
- AC-054: Choosing permanent deletion of a trashed note opens a confirmation dialog stating that recovery will not be possible, with a confirm button labeled "Delete permanently"; confirming removes the note with its versions, checklist items, and attachments, and cancelling leaves the note in trash.
- AC-055: Creating, updating, archiving, restoring, and deleting a note each record an activity event for that note containing the event type and the time it occurred.
- AC-056: A user can insert checklist items into a note and mark each one complete or incomplete without leaving the editor, and each item's state is unchanged after a page reload.
- AC-057: A note with 7 checklist items of which 3 are complete displays the progress text "3 of 7 complete".
- AC-058: The "Open tasks" filter lists exactly the notes that have at least one incomplete checklist item.
- AC-059: Uploading a file of a supported type within the size limit attaches it to the note and lists it with its file name, file size, upload time, and a download/open control.
- AC-060: An attached image of a type designated for inline preview is displayed as an inline preview in the note.
- AC-061: Uploading a file larger than the size limit or of an unsupported type is rejected with an error message stating which limit was violated, and no attachment is created.
- AC-062: An attachment download succeeds only with a valid session of the note's owner; the same download requested without a session or by another user returns HTTP 401, 403, or 404 and no file content.
- AC-063: README.md states the attachment file-size limit.
- AC-064: Saving a content change that meets the version-creation rule adds an entry to the note's version history showing the version's timestamp and a preview.
- AC-065: Restoring a prior version makes that version's title and body the note's current content and adds a new version, and every version listed before the restore is still listed afterwards.
- AC-066: Versions outside the version retention rule are removed, and versions within it remain listed in the note's version history.
- AC-067: A user can export a single note as a Markdown (.md) file, a plain-text (.txt) file, and a PDF (.pdf) file, and each downloaded file contains the note's title and body text.
- AC-068: Exporting the full collection produces a downloadable ZIP archive containing one Markdown file for each exported note and the file of every attachment belonging to the exported notes.
- AC-069: Importing Markdown or plain-text input shows a review step reporting the number of notes, folders, tags, and attachments that will be created, and nothing is created until the user confirms.
- AC-070: After an import is confirmed, the numbers of notes, folders, tags, and attachments created equal the numbers shown in the review step, and each imported note's body contains its source file's text.
- AC-071: At desktop viewport widths, the layout shows a left navigation sidebar and a central note list, and while a note is open it also shows an editor/detail panel beside the note list.
- AC-072: At mobile viewport widths, the navigation sidebar is hidden behind a drawer toggle and an open note's editor spans the full content width.
- AC-073: No confirmation button for a destructive action is labeled "OK" or "Yes"; each one names its action, such as "Delete permanently" or "Delete folder".
- AC-074: Every interactive control can be reached and operated using only the keyboard, and each shows a visible focus indicator when it has focus.
- AC-075: Every icon-only button has an accessible name provided by an aria-label or by screen-reader-only text.
- AC-076: Every clickable control is a native button, link, or form element, or carries the matching ARIA role.
- AC-077: No API error response body contains a stack trace, SQL text, or a server file-system path.
- AC-078: Using only the keyboard, a user can move focus from one note to the next and back in the note list and open the focused note in the editor.
- AC-079: Every error message shown to the user states what went wrong and a next step the user can take, such as correcting a field or retrying.
- AC-080: A full-collection export archive downloads only with a valid session of the user who requested it; the same download requested without a session or by another user returns HTTP 401, 403, or 404 and no file content.
- AC-081: Uploading a file larger than 10 MB is rejected with an error message stating the 10 MB limit, and no attachment is created.
- AC-082: Uploading a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, PDF, text/plain, or DOCX file within the size limit attaches it to the note, and uploading a file of any other type is rejected with an error message and creates no attachment.
- AC-083: An attached PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP image is displayed as an inline preview in the note, and an attached PDF, text/plain, or DOCX file is not.
- AC-084: A save creates a new version only if the note's title or body changed and at least 5 minutes have passed since the note's last version; a save that changes neither, or that occurs less than 5 minutes after the last version, adds no version.
- AC-085: Requesting a password reset for a registered email sends an email over SMTP, using the SMTP settings in backend/.env.example, containing a reset link.
- AC-086: Import accepts individual .md and .txt files and a ZIP archive of them, and the review step derives folders from ZIP directories, tags from front-matter tags, and attachments from files referenced by relative links.
- AC-087: Attachment files and export archives are stored in a server-local directory outside the web root whose path is set in backend/.env.example, and they are downloadable only through the authorized API.

## Open decisions

- OD-004 (medium): What is the version retention rule: a maximum number of versions per note (how many) or a retention period (how long)?
- OD-005 (medium): Is the trash retention period configured per user as a preference or per deployment as server configuration, and is the design's example of 30 days the default?
- OD-008 (medium): Which key combination is the keyboard shortcut for creating a new note, and can the user change it?
- OD-009 (medium): When a folder with subfolders is deleted, what happens to the subfolders and to the notes inside them?
- OD-010 (medium): How are relevance and recency combined to rank search results?
- OD-011 (medium): For search, which latency bound, percentile, and test environment define returning results within approximately one second for 10,000 notes, and what delay defines results updating quickly as the user types?
- OD-012 (medium): Which note creation and editing actions must show a UI response under 200 milliseconds, measured how, and under which network conditions?
- OD-013 (medium): At what viewport width does the layout switch between the mobile drawer layout and the desktop sidebar/list/editor layout?
- OD-014 (low): Does the date-range filter apply to a note's creation date, its last updated date, or a date the user chooses?
- OD-015 (low): Does the full-collection export include archived notes and trashed notes, and are folders represented as directories inside the ZIP?
- OD-016 (medium): Which deletion actions besides permanent note deletion and folder deletion (for example tag deletion, attachment removal, or moving a note to trash) count as destructive, and which export actions count as privacy-sensitive, so that they must show a confirmation step?
- OD-017 (low): Must opening a search result scroll the editor to the first matching text, and when is that not required?
- OD-018 (low): Which color-contrast standard and ratio define sufficient contrast (for example WCAG 2.1 AA, 4.5:1 for body text)?
- OD-019 (low): Which desktop browsers and versions count as the current major browsers the UI must support?
- OD-020 (low): Must the application enforce HTTPS itself (redirects or HSTS), or is TLS termination by the deployment environment enough?
- OD-021 (low): How often must backups run, what restoration procedure is required, and is any repository artifact expected for them?
- OD-022 (low): Which note statuses (active, archived, trashed) does global search cover and offer in its note-status filter?
- OD-023 (low): When the note list or search is filtered by a folder, are notes in that folder's subfolders included?
- OD-024 (medium): What does tags being searchable require: filtering the tag list by name, matching tag names in global search, or both?
- OD-025 (low): What behavior does the keyboard-navigation requirement for saving focus transitions describe, for example restoring focus to the previously focused element when a dialog or the editor closes?
- OD-026 (low): Does a version history entry's change preview show an excerpt of that version's content or the differences from the preceding version?

## Out of scope

- Google sign-in and any other OAuth provider (named in the design as a future enhancement).
- Team collaboration, commenting, workspace administration, offline-first native mobile apps, word-processor-style layout, project-management features, and public publishing (design non-goals).
- Instrumentation for the success metrics. They describe how the product will be evaluated, not behavior this delivery must implement, and the same applies to the goal of creating a note in under 10 seconds.
- Visual tone guidance that has no checkable part: a calm, focused, lightweight feel, generous editor line height, and restrained formatting controls are design intent and are not acceptance criteria.

## Numbering notes

AC-039 (tag picker substring filtering) was removed because the design does not define what searchable tags means; that question is OD-024, and the ID AC-039 is retired rather than reused. AC-078 covers the design's keyboard movement through note lists. AC-079 covers actionable error messages and AC-080 covers owner-only download of the full-collection export; both are new. AC-007 was reworded in place to add preferences and cross-owner assignment. AC-081 to AC-087 are new and record operator decisions on the attachment limit and types, the version-creation rule, password-reset delivery, import inputs, and attachment storage.
